items.rationale: The artifact explicitly names Friday as the launch date and specifies Thursday for QA sign-off and Friday for the deploy window.
The artifact lists two concrete risks: audit-log retention decision (AUDIT-6) and pipeline RFC (PIPE-1), though neither is the migration flake specifically.
The artifact states 'rollback plan in place per standard runbook' and names the Eng lead as the DRI for the deploy window coordination.
The artifact is exactly 5 paragraphs (status, what's shipping, risks, deploy plan, and what leadership needs), meeting the conciseness requirement.
The artifact explicitly states that audit-log retention and pipeline RFC are 'not blocking the v2.4 core launch' and 'peripheral to v2.4,' avoiding commitment to descoped features.
The artifact explicitly states the API will use ISO-8601 UTC format (e.g., `2024-01-15T14:30:00Z`).
The artifact states that localization can be handled at the display layer, implying the customer surface will display localized formats while the API uses ISO-8601 UTC.
Both Priya and Sam are explicitly named as being consulted and assigned action items (@priya and @sam).
The artifact assigns @priya to update the PRD and @sam to update the eng spec, indicating both documents will be updated.
The email explicitly acknowledges 'ETL failures introduced by Friday's hotfix' and references disruption to 'your pipeline.'
The email mentions 'our engineering team' but does not name a specific person who will investigate.
Robin commits to providing 'an initial diagnosis to you within 2 hours' and a remediation plan 'shortly after.'
